source.citation: Unidentified author (New York Polyclinic), article on sulfonal, Case VI, Medical Record 33 (1888): 416. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

complaints: attacks of neuralgic pain all through the body, worst at night
presentation.course: Under treatment for several years for many neurasthenic and hysterical symptoms. Still sleepless while away in the mountains.
presentation.priorTreatment: Frequent chloral, morphine, and other narcotics, with little success.

treatments.response: slept five hours for three nights, then the drug lost its effect entirely

quotes: under treat- ment for several years for all sorts of neurasthenic and hysterical symptoms
after that, drug lost its effects entirely

modernReading.text: Chronic widespread pain and insomnia, with tolerance to several sedatives. The cause cannot be known from this record; a modern doctor would think of chronic pain, depression, and dependence on hypnotics and opiates.

fixed: has tried chloral and morphine; new drugs work briefly

constrained.rule: comfortable or better; has been to the mountains for her health
she may be more interested in a new drug than in other advice

notes: A patient who has seen many doctors. A useful contrast with the merchant on the same page, whom the same drug helped.
